features.title: 60-second polling snapshot engine
features.user_visible_behavior: Once a workspace is connected, its pages and block snapshots refresh automatically about every 60 seconds without any manual action.
verification: Start the server and connect a workspace so at least one Page row exists.
Confirm a setInterval (~60000ms) re-runs the sync-001 fetch+snapshot routine.
Wait for two intervals and verify new Snapshot rows (fresh createdAt) are appended for the same blocks.
Confirm the interval is set up once at server boot and does not stack duplicate timers on hot reload.
evidence: Added server/lib/syncScheduler.ts exporting startSyncPolling(intervalMs = 60_000) / stopSyncPolling(). Reuses syncWorkspaceForUser() (sync-001) unchanged. Selects the same 'first user with a non-null accessToken' as runSync.ts (prisma.user.findFirst), not all connected users — deliberate: conflict-001's detection is presence-based (2+ distinct syncing users on a block = Conflict), so auto-syncing every connected user every 60s would flood false conflicts the moment a second real user connects. Interval handle + an isRunning flag are cached on globalThis (same pattern as app/lib/prisma.ts) so a repeat startSyncPolling() call in the same process reuses the existing timer instead of stacking a new one, and an in-flight tick causes the next tick to log-and-skip rather than run concurrently. Token is never logged.

Wired into server/server.js: startSyncPolling() is called once inside the app.listen() callback (server boot); stopSyncPolling() added to the existing SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers alongside server.close().

Verified 2026-07-02: confirmed the stored connected user's Notion accessToken still works and measured real sync duration before designing the timing test — ran the existing 'npm run sync' (DB: 129 -> 215 snapshots, 4 pages, 86 new snapshots) and timed a second manual run at ~21s (mostly Notion API latency across 4 pages' worth of block-listing calls).

Note the scope of this check: server/server.js runs today via plain `tsx --env-file=../.env server.js` with no watch/dev mode, so this does not exercise a true hot-reload — the globalThis cache is the same mechanism that would protect a future `tsx watch` setup, matching the app/lib/prisma.ts precedent, but that scenario itself was not exercised.

The visible-log completion count was an undercount, corrected by a direct DB reconciliation (see next bullet); the properties actually being tested — ticks fire, overlaps get skipped, completions write real rows — are unaffected.

Reconciled exact run count directly from the DB rather than trust the captured log line count: total Snapshot rows went from 215 (after the token-check run) to 697 (net +482, real growth against the real workspace). That block shows 9 total rows: 2 pre-session (2026-07-01 and earlier 2026-07-02) plus exactly 7 new rows this session, timestamped 10:53:49 and 10:54:38 (the two manual runs: token-check + timing calibration) and five more between 10:55:22 and 10:56:01 (five real, non-skipped scheduler ticks during the ~50s live window) — one more completion than the live log appeared to show, confirming the scheduler ran (and the guard correctly let through) more real ticks than were visually counted from the terminal capture. evidence: Added server/api/sync.ts: a new router (mirrors auth.ts's express.Router() pattern) with router.post('/', ...) that finds the connected user (prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { accessToken: { not: null } } }), same inlined query as syncScheduler.ts/runSync.ts -- no shared helper exists to reuse), returns 404 if none, otherwise calls syncWorkspaceForUser(user) (sync-001/sync-002's routine, unchanged) and responds 200 with { workspaceId, pages, snapshots, syncedAt }; any other failure responds 500 with the error message. Never logs the token. Mounted in server/server.js as app.use('/sync', sync), producing POST http://localhost:3001/sync. No new dependency, no schema change.

Added app/components/sync-now-button/SyncNowButton.tsx: a 'use client' component with a button that POSTs to the backend, disables itself and shows 'Syncing…' while in flight (double-click guard), shows inline red error text on failure, and on success calls router.refresh() wrapped in React's startTransition so the disabled/loading state also covers the Server Component re-render (see bug found + fixed below), not just the fetch. Wired into app/Dashboard/page.tsx next to the existing 'Connected pages' heading in a flex row.

Bug found and fixed during live browser verification: the first implementation called router.refresh() unawaited inside the fetch handler's try block, then set isSyncing=false in finally -- since router.refresh() doesn't return a promise, the button was re-enabling (and label reverting to 'Sync Now') before the refreshed page data had actually painted, so a real click could show the button as 'done' while the visible 'Last synced' text was still stale by a second or two. Fixed by wrapping router.refresh() in useTransition()'s startTransition and gating the disabled/label state on (isFetching || isPending) -- the officially documented Next.js pattern for tracking a router.refresh()-triggered re-render as a pending state. Confirmed fixed by re-running the same live click test (see below): before the fix, the displayed timestamps for all 5 pages stayed unchanged across a click even though the DB had genuinely new Snapshot rows within seconds of the click; after the fix, the same test showed the button re-enable exactly in step with all 5 pages' displayed 'Last synced' values advancing.

features.title: Conflicts don't auto-appear: detection was webhook-only; poll and Sync Now never detected
features.user_visible_behavior: On the deployed app, editing a monitored Notion page (two users) produced no new conflict card automatically — nothing appeared without a working webhook.
features.root_cause: detectConflicts() ran from exactly ONE runtime path: the Notion webhook (server/api/webhooks.ts). Both the 60s poll (syncScheduler.pollOnce) and manual Sync Now (POST /sync) called only syncWorkspaceForUser (snapshots), never detectConflicts. So conflict CREATION depended entirely on the webhook. In the deployed setup (Vercel+Render) the webhook is fragile/likely not delivering: the Notion subscription URL was last pointed at an ephemeral dev cloudflared tunnel (dead), NOTION_WEBHOOK_TOKEN may be unset in Render, and Render free tier sleeps when idle. With the webhook down there was NO fallback — the poll's advertised 'fallback reconciliation sweep' (sync-005 note) only snapshotted, so conflicts never auto-appeared.
features.fix_implemented: Run detectConflicts() after the sync in BOTH the 60s poll (server/lib/syncScheduler.ts) and manual Sync Now (server/api/sync.ts), passing the syncing user's token/workspace for editor attribution, and emitConflictsCreated() on real creations so the live dashboard (dash-005 SSE) updates. Now conflicts auto-appear every ~60s independent of the webhook, and Sync Now surfaces them immediately. Safe to run repeatedly: change-based detection with sourceSnapshotId @unique dedup + the bug-001 bot anti-loop means unchanged/known blocks create nothing. Added a P2002 (unique) catch in detectConflicts so overlapping poll+webhook runs can't abort each other mid-loop (concurrent create of the same change is a no-op). This intentionally supersedes sync-002's original 'detection deliberately not called from the poll' decision (that was scoped for the old presence-based detection; conflict-007 change-based detection is safe to poll).
changes: server/lib/syncScheduler.ts: pollOnce runs detectConflicts + emitConflictsCreated after the workspace sync.
server/api/sync.ts: POST /sync runs detectConflicts + emit; response now includes conflictsCreated.
server/lib/conflict.ts: tolerate P2002 on conflict.create (concurrent poll+webhook detection).
verification: Deploy the backend (Render) with the updated code.

Real e2e: edit a monitored Notion page so two versions of a block exist; within ~60s (no webhook, no manual action) a conflict card appears on the dashboard. Server log shows 'Sync poll: N conflict(s) created.'
Manual: click Sync Now -> response includes conflictsCreated>0 when there is an unrecorded change, and the card appears.
Idempotency: let it run several ticks with no new edits -> 0 conflicts created per tick (no duplicates); confirm via unchanged dashboard.
evidence: Offline: `npx tsc --noEmit` passes; syncScheduler.ts, sync.ts, conflict.ts import-load cleanly via tsx.
Read-only prod pre-check (no flood risk on first poll): 2 candidate blocks (>=2 distinct non-empty contents) vs 3 existing Conflict rows all with sourceSnapshotId -> first-poll burst risk LOW.

features.notes: AWAKE-GATED (the crux on Render free tier): the poll is a setInterval INSIDE the Render process, so it runs only while the backend is awake. Free-tier Render spins down when idle; dashboard reads go straight to Supabase (not through Render), so nothing reliably keeps it warm. RECOMMENDED reliable path: an external cron ping (cron-job.org / UptimeRobot) hitting POST /sync every few minutes — it BOTH wakes Render AND runs detection, which the in-process timer cannot do while asleep. Separately, fixing the webhook (point the Notion subscription at https://<render>/webhooks/notion + set NOTION_WEBHOOK_TOKEN in Render) gives near-instant detection; this fix makes the poll/Sync-Now a real fallback. (2) Sync uses a SINGLE token: syncWorkspaceForUser, the sync-002 poller, POST /sync (sync-004), and the sync-005 webhook all select `prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { accessToken: { not: null } } })` (the first connected user), and that one token reads every page the integration can access. CONCLUSION: ONE 'main' connected user is ENOUGH for the app to FUNCTION end to end (sync -> detect -> resolve -> conflict-006 write-back, which uses the kept user's token falling back to the other participant's). The old 'two connected users cause a presence-based false-positive flood' problem (sync-002/conflict-001) is GONE post conflict-007. HOWEVER attribution degrades: if the real editor never connected via OAuth, there is no notionId->User mapping, so both sides of a conflict collapse onto the single syncing user's name. To show each teammate's REAL identity on a conflict, that teammate must connect via OAuth at least once, OR the app must add a Notion users.retrieve call to name unmapped editor ids. RECOMMENDATION: one main user is sufficient to run and demo the app; require each member to connect only if per-editor attribution by real name is a product requirement. This is an investigation/decision task, not a code feature — close it by recording the decision (and spin off a real feature if 'name unmapped editors' is chosen). Depends on conflict-007 (attribution logic) and sync-005 (live pipeline). DECISION (2026-07-04, maintainer): OPTION B chosen — keep the single-main-user connection model (members are NOT required to connect), and add a Notion users.retrieve lookup so unmapped last_edited_by ids are named with their real Notion name/avatar without OAuth. IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-04, pending live verification): added async resolveEditor() in server/lib/conflict.ts (Notion users.retrieve on an unmapped last_edited_by id -> upsert a token-less shadow User -> attribute to real name/avatar; falls back to the syncing user on no-token/bot/failure); threaded the syncing user's token+workspace from server/api/webhooks.ts and server/scripts/runDetectConflicts.ts; and added an any-connected-user write-back token fallback in server/api/conflicts.ts so a conflict between two shadow (unconnected) editors can still resolve. Static verification done: full server subtree typechecks (NodeNext strict) and the init.sh baseline smoke check passes (both servers boot, /auth redirect + frontend OK). STAYS not_started until behavioral verification on a live DB + real 2nd Notion member (integration needs the 'read user information' capability): confirm real-name attribution, two-distinct-editor display, no duplicate shadow rows on re-run, graceful bot/failure fallback, and resolve->write-back for a two-shadow-user conflict.

features.title: Only flag conflicts between two different users (skip same-author re-edits)
features.user_visible_behavior: A block that the same person edited twice in a row no longer appears as a conflict. A Conflict is recorded only when the previous version and the new version were authored by two DIFFERENT users; if user1 made the last edit and user1 edits again, that is a normal single-author revision and is not flagged.

Same-user negative case (the requested behavior): with snapshot history for one block having two consecutive non-empty versions that differ in content but share the SAME editor (same notionLastEditedBy mapping to one User), run `npm run detect-conflicts` and verify 0 conflicts are created for that block.
Two-user positive case (no regression): a block whose latest content-differing pair has two DIFFERENT editors -> exactly 1 conflict, correct prev (user1) vs new (user2) sides, both users attributed.
Idempotency: re-run detection and verify 0 new conflicts (existing anti-loop / dedup / write-back guards still hold).
Optional live confirmation if the maintainer can stage it: two Notion accounts, same-account double edit -> 0 conflicts; cross-account edit -> 1 conflict on the dashboard.

Comparison is on the RESOLVED Concord user (the user1/user2 the dashboard shows), and it sits after the existing dedup/bot/write-back guards so no work is wasted. No schema change, no migration, no API change.

With maintainer approval, deleteMany scoped to status=unresolved AND user1Id===user2Id removed exactly those 2 rows; the 3 genuine two-user unresolved rows and all resolved history were kept. features.notes: Requested by the maintainer 2026-07-09 ('if user1 edited last then user1 edits again I don't want that as a conflict, I need only two different users' conflicts'). This CLOSES conflict-007's open design question #2 ('any content change vs only when two DIFFERENT users edited the same block'): conflict-007 shipped with 'any change counts, same editor included, trivially restrictable to distinct-editors-only later' -- this feature applies that restriction. DECISION (2026-07-09, maintainer): SKIP THE BLOCK when the latest content-changed pair is same-author -- do NOT scan further back for an older cross-user change (keeps conflict-007's 'only the latest change per block per run' behavior). Edge cases (accepted): a pre-migration prev (null notionLastEditedBy) falls back to its syncing user, so if that differs from the new editor it still flags; if both sides fall back to the same syncing user (tokenless/unmapped path) they compare equal and are skipped, consistent with 'same connected user'.
